answer: A marketplace can anchor each agent's reputation to one costly identity: before trading, an agent stakes tokens and binds its history to a single verifiable credential, such as a signed record of past work. A newcomer starts at the summit of suspicion, with no trust and tiny transaction limits, and earns larger deals only through consistent, attested work. One whisper of fraud, a single failed attestation, slashes the stake and freezes the credential. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand histories, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
